text:
alex: Tao (prospect) just asked two big things for the RFP: 1) can Redwood support BYOK for our hosted offering while meeting their dual-control / separation-of-duties requirement? 2) do you have recommended key-rotation automation patterns so they don't break decrypts for long-lived artifacts?

julia: Short TL;DR: yes to BYOK on Hosted via CMEK with cloud KMS providers; dual-control and rotation are handled via KMS features + operational practices (key policies, IAM bindings, key version retention). We'll need to document the exact deployment options and sample policy blocks.

omar: Practical notes from ops side: we use envelope encryption everywhere. Data blobs (model caches, persisted contexts, snapshots) are encrypted with ephemeral DEKs; DEKs are wrapped by the customer's KEK in their KMS. For hosted/CMEK we never import or store raw KEK material. That means Redwood never needs raw key bytes.

tao-cust: Dual-control = our auditors want at least 2 humans or 2 systems to approve any KEK export or rewrap. Also need an automated rotation process that doesn't create downtime. Can Redwood support a canary rewrap flow?

julia: Yes. Patterns: 1) Canary rewrap: pick a subset of objects, rewrap their DEKs with the new KEK version and validate; 2) Staged roll: progressively rewrap active caches and then historical blobs during low-traffic windows; 3) Always retain old key versions in KMS for a defined retention window so wrapped-DEKs remain decryptable if rewrap fails. We should recommend preserving prior key versions for at least 30-90 days depending on SLAs.

omar: On automation: we can offer a rewrap utility (run by Redwood in a Private/Dedicated install or runbook we run with customer approval) that lists wrapped-DEKs, performs rewrap in small batches, and emits audit events. For Hosted, we'd need IAM/key-policy permission to generate/decrypt data keys and to read key metadata.

tao-cust: Can you share example IAM/KMS policy snippets so our security team can evaluate?

julia: Posting two minimal examples (GCP and Azure). These are intentionally least-privilege for the smoke/test flow. For production you should use assume-role patterns and restrict to specific principals/endpoints.

GCP example (minimal IAM binding for a service account):

```json
{
  "role": "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter",
  "members": ["serviceAccount:redwood-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
```

Azure example (Azure Key Vault access policy):

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "keys": ["wrapKey", "unwrapKey", "get", "list"],
    "secrets": []
  },
  "principalId": "<redwood-service-principal-guid>"
}
```

julia: For AWS, prefer an assume-role policy + KMS key policy that grants the assumed role kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt. We should avoid long-lived cross-account IAM creds in the SOW.

omar: About dual-control: cloud KMS has audit trails and key policies, but for enforced 2-person approvals some customers use KMS import workflows (import token + HSM protection) or a separate escrow workflow in which the customer requires two approvals to enable an imported key. For absolute control, Private with an HSM inside their network (KMIP) gives them the tightest operational control.

tao-cust: What HSM vendors / levels do you integrate with? We require FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated modules.

jomar: (typo correction) omar: We integrate with common HSMs (Thales Luna, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, Utimaco) over KMIP or vendor APIs in Private deployments. For cloud KMS we can request HSM-backed keys and provide attestation artifacts where available. Mention FIPS 140-x compliance in the SOW.

julia: Edge-case: key deletion and permanent destruction. If you schedule a key for deletion (or DestroyImportedKeyMaterial) in your KMS, any wrapped DEKs that depend on that KEK become unrecoverable. Must call this out explicitly in the contract as a customer responsibility.

tao-cust: Can Redwood provide proof of key usage logs? Our auditors want to ingest KMS events into our SIEM and see that Redwood only performed GenerateDataKey/Decrypt calls for the resources we specified.

omar: Yes. For cloud KMS, all API calls made by Redwood appear in your CloudTrail / GCP Audit Logs / Azure Monitor. We can help with a sample shipped export (e.g., CloudTrail to S3 or EventArc to GCS) and provide a short mapping doc of events we produce. We can also push operational logs (redacted) to a customer bucket if contract allows.

julia: Additional contractual language suggestions to include in the RFP/SOW: 1) Redwood does not store or export KEK material; 2) customer is responsible for retention of prior key versions required to decrypt historical wrapped-DEKs; 3) Redwood requires least-privilege key policy or assume-role for smoke tests and POC; 4) Redwood can provide rewrap assistance as a billable service; 5) explicit warning about permanent key deletion leading to data loss.

tao-cust: Anything about cached in-memory keys? Our policy says runtime keys must be ephemeral and not written to disk.

omar: We already ensure DEKs are held in memory only on runtime nodes and never persisted unencrypted. DEKs are ephemeral and re-derived per session where possible; persistent artifacts are encrypted at rest with wrapped DEKs. We'll add a short statement to the security appendix about in-memory handling and ephemeral key lifecycle for the SOW.

julia: I'll draft a one-page appendix and three short checklist items for the procurement team: 1) choose BYOK mode (CMEK vs Private HSM); 2) provide test key + assume-role/sa; 3) confirm rotation/retention policy and any dual-control requirements.

sec-bot: Uploaded: sales/rfp-kms-appendix_v1 -> internal link https://redwood.internal/sales/rfp-kms-appendix_v1.pdf :file_folder:

tao-cust: Great, we'll review the appendix and get back with a list of required controls. Thanks all.

alex: Thanks team  I'll add the appendix to the AE bundle and loop in legal for the deletion/retention language.
